name: etcd
model: Small ordered key-value store with revisions, range reads, watches on keys, leases (TTL) and compare-and-swap transactions
engine_note: Raft-replicated log applied to bbolt, a memory-mapped B+tree file; every change gets a global revision number
consistency: Strictly serializable key-value operations: reads are linearizable by default (serializable, possibly stale, as an option); multi-key If/Then/Else transactions are atomic; a write is durable on a Raft majority before acknowledgment.

jepsen.finding: Reads could be stale because a node that believed it was leader answered from local state; etcd then added a quorum=true read option, and v3 made linearizable reads the default.
Key-value operations and watches were strictly serializable under faults; etcd locks cannot guarantee mutual exclusion, which was poorly documented (docs partly improved).
The Java client retried non-idempotent requests, so transactions could run twice (lost updates); a client bug, not in etcd, with no patch at publication; workaround is disabling retries.

scaling: Does not shard: every node holds all data and writes go through one Raft leader. Default storage quota 2 GiB, about 8 GiB suggested maximum.
managed: Hidden inside managed Kubernetes control planes (Amazon EKS, Google GKE, Azure AKS); no major standalone etcd service
reach: Reach for it for small, critical coordination data: configuration, service discovery, leader election, feature flags that many machines must agree on.
avoid: Avoid for application data, anything over a few GB, high write rates, or as a lock for correctness without fencing tokens.
escape: You need many machines to agree on a little configuration, with watches, and survive a node loss.
chat: Nothing for chat data; at most the cluster config or leader election for the services that serve it.
notes: The 2014 aphyr post does not name an etcd version in its text (unconfirmed). A reader comment (2014-07-11) notes etcd merged a quorum=true fix. aphyr.com is blocked from this network (HTTP 451); date read from a Wayback Machine copy. Storage limits per etcd docs (2 GiB default quota via --quota-backend-bytes; 8 GiB suggested max). The Kubernetes managed-control-plane claim is general knowledge; the cited Kubernetes page only says etcd is the cluster's backing store.
